name: Peter Thomas
profile: Welsh businessman who, with brother Sir Stanley Thomas, built Peter's Pies (sold to Grand Metropolitan in 1988) and later property/transport interests; former Cardiff Rugby chairman and benefactor, CBE 2012. Died 29 March 2023, aged 79.
notes: Deceased: died 29 March 2023 aged 79 (Cardiff Rugby / Caerphilly Observer: https://caerphilly.observer/news/1018781/bedwas-based-peters-pies-pays-tribute-to-peter-thomas/). Surviving brother Sir Stanley Thomas shared the Rich List entry.

name: AM Arun
profile: Dr A.M. Arun founded and chaired Vasan Healthcare / Vasan Eye Care, a Chennai-based eye-hospital chain. Died of cardiac arrest in Chennai on 16 November 2020, aged 51.

name: Lady Smith
current_role: Co-founder figure behind the Paul Smith fashion label; wife of Sir Paul Smith
profile: Pauline, Lady Smith (née Denyer) is the wife of designer Sir Paul Smith and shares his Rich List entry (fashion). A Royal College of Art-trained fashion designer, she helped him launch his first Nottingham shop in 1970, which grew into a brand with ~130 stores in 60+ countries. Very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She was a Royal College of Art-trained fashion designer teaching at a Nottingham art school when she met Paul Smith; she married him when he was 21.
deep_cut_fact: Before the Paul Smith label existed, her RCA fashion training contributed to many of the pieces sold at the Nottingham boutique Paul managed for six years, and Paul has credited her with teaching him garment construction.
notes: Very private; no personal channels. Email is for Paul Smith's Foundation (Sir Paul's archive charity, Nottingham), the closest published route. Sources disagree on wedding date (1967 per Wikipedia vs 2000 per other profiles), so avoid citing it. No death reported, but status not confirmed.

name: Michael Donald Schoeb
current_role: CEO and Director, Alliance Laundry Holdings Inc. (NYSE: ALH)
profile: Mike Schoeb joined Alliance Laundry Systems (Ripon, Wisconsin; maker of Speed Queen commercial washers/dryers) as President & COO in 2007 and became CEO in 2011. He led the company through its October 2025 NYSE IPO (~$826M base deal), and his wealth stems from his ALH equity. Earlier roles at Wausau Homes, Hilti and Johnson Controls.
interesting_fact: Alliance Laundry says its enterprise value has quadrupled during his tenure as CEO; the company claims roughly 40% of the North American commercial laundry market and went public on the NYSE on 8 Oct 2025 at $22/share.
deep_cut_fact: Before laundry, he ran Hilti's Brazilian business as President of Hilti do Brasil and was Hilti's SVP of Marketing & Brand for North America, after starting out in sales/general management at Johnson Controls.
notes: Public-company CEO; best route is via Alliance Laundry IR/corporate communications. Education per 2007 release: MBA and MS from Johns Hopkins, BA political science from Mount St. Mary's (Emmitsburg, MD).

name: Keith Bradshaw
current_role: Chairman and 50% co-owner, Listers Group (car dealerships, Stratford-upon-Avon); co-owner/non-exec chairman, Nurton Developments
profile: Aston-born chartered accountant who built BP Nursing Homes into Takare plc, Europe's largest care-home operator (14,000 staff), selling it to BUPA in 1998 for ~£300m. Co-founded Listers car dealership in Coventry with Terry Lister in 1979; it is now England's largest independent dealer group (£1.2bn+ turnover). Also co-owns Birmingham developer Nurton.
interesting_fact: Listers grew from a single dealership and body shop in Coventry into a 50+ outlet group selling BMW, Land Rover, Jaguar, Audi, Toyota, Mercedes and more, with Terry Lister as its public face.
deep_cut_fact: After qualifying as an accountant in Birmingham in 1966 he spent time working in West Africa, returning at 30 to start the companies that became Takare. He is also deputy chairman and co-owner of Laney/Headstock, the amp and musical-instrument maker, and chaired the trustees of the Library of Birmingham.
notes: Was 74 in 2018 (now ~82); low-profile, Terry Lister is Listers' public face. Was High Sheriff of the West Midlands 2016-17. Son David runs Nurton Developments. No published personal email found.

name: Chris Miller
current_role: Co-owner, Harris & Sheldon Group (Meriden, property/investment/sporting estates); co-founder and former executive vice-chairman of Melrose Industries (stood down March 2024)
profile: Christopher Miller worked for Lord Hanson and was chief executive of engineering group Wassall before co-founding Melrose Industries in 2003 with David Roper and Simon Peckham; Melrose's 'buy, improve, sell' model culminated in the GKN takeover. With brother Michael he owns family group Harris & Sheldon, now focused on investments, property and sporting lets.
interesting_fact: Melrose floated on AIM in 2003 with a market cap of just £10m and grew into a FTSE 100 group via deals for McKechnie, FKI, Elster, Nortek and GKN before refocusing on aerospace in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Through Harris & Sheldon the Miller brothers own the Junction Pool on the River Tweed near Kelso, one of Scotland's most famous salmon beats and said to be a favourite of the Queen Mother, plus the Taymount beats on the Tay; the group once owned Hardy fishing tackle and Webley & Scott air rifles.
notes: Step-down from Melrose announced Sept 2023, effective March 2024 (https://www.thebusinessdesk.com/westmidlands/?p=2077477). Harris & Sheldon is based at Packington Hall; no published email found. Shares Rich List entry with brother Michael Miller.

name: Kenneth L. Cornick
current_role: Director, Clarivate plc (since July 2025); co-founder and major shareholder of CLEAR (Clear Secure), former President/CFO
profile: Ken Cornick co-founded value-focused hedge fund Arience Capital (~$1bn AUM) with Caryn Seidman Becker, then in 2010 the pair bought bankrupt Verified Identity Pass and relaunched it as CLEAR, the biometric airport-identity company (NYSE: YOU, IPO 2021). He was President and CFO until 31 March 2025, then an adviser; he now sits on Clarivate's board.
interesting_fact: CLEAR was rebuilt from a bankruptcy-auction purchase of Verified Identity Pass in 2010 into a public company whose biometric lanes operate across US airports and stadiums.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2018 PYMNTS interview he summed up CLEAR's thesis: 'going forward, security demands are going to grow, not diminish — and identity is a key element of security.' He also testified as CLEAR's president before a US Senate Commerce subcommittee in 2019.
notes: Left CLEAR executive roles 31 Mar 2025 and did not stand for re-election to CLEAR's board (SEC 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1856314/000185631425000006/exhibit992-clearannouncesl.htm); CLEAR IR is only an indirect route. Bowdoin BA. Low personal media profile.

name: Chester Hunt
profile: Appears on the Sunday Times Rich List 2020 jointly as 'Michael and Chester Hunt and family' (car sales and property). Michael Hunt made his fortune helping build the £1bn Nissan UK car-import operation; Chester Hunt appears to be a family member, but no public profile of him could be found.
interesting_fact: The Hunt family fortune originated in Nissan UK, which the 2016 Sunday Times Rich List described as a £1bn car operation built by Michael Hunt.
notes: No independent web presence found for 'Chester Hunt'; relationship to Michael Hunt is inferred from the joint Rich List entry only. Do not conflate with Foxtons founder Jon Hunt. Recommend skipping or approaching via family business if identified.

name: Lee Biggins
current_role: Founder and CEO, CV-Library (UK job board, Fleet, Hampshire)
profile: Lee Biggins left school at 15, worked in his father's carpet-fitting business, and in 2000 co-founded job board CV-Library with school friend Brian Wakem on a £9,000 bank loan. He bought out Wakem's 50% for ~£10m in 2013 and has owned 100% since; CV-Library became one of the UK's largest job sites and launched US sister site Resume-Library in 2015. He moved from MD to CEO in 2019.
interesting_fact: He had no computer skills when he had the idea at 19: he bought an £899 PC and an internet how-to book, took a computer literacy course in Fleet, and asked at his local pub whether anyone could build a website, which is how he found co-founder Brian Wakem.
deep_cut_fact: CV-Library's first marketing push, putting flyers on every car parked outside Fleet railway station, flopped; it only took off after switching to search-engine ads, and for its first three years he kept working in his dad's carpet business and did shifts at a recruitment agency to learn the industry.
notes: Regular media commentator on the UK jobs market (e.g. City AM contributor profile https://www.cityam.com/profile/lee-biggins/), so likely receptive to a founder-story podcast. Only press email found is a 2014 named staffer address, not included as likely stale.

name: Aman Mehta
current_role: Managing Director, Torrent Pharmaceuticals Ltd (since 1 Aug 2025)
profile: Aman Mehta is the third-generation heir of Ahmedabad's Torrent Group (pharma and power) and son of chairman Samir Mehta. Educated at Boston University (economics) and Columbia (MBA), he joined the group in 2013, worked across both power and pharma, ran Torrent Pharma's India business (its largest revenue driver), joined the board in 2022 and became MD in August 2025.
interesting_fact: He has held roles in both of Torrent's verticals, power and pharma, which makes him a relevant voice for an energy-focused podcast; Torrent Power is one of India's major private integrated utilities.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming MD he led the integration of Torrent's Unichem and Curatio Healthcare acquisitions, turned around the company's cardiac and diabetes portfolio, and launched a consumer-health division.
notes: Hurun listed him 2018-19, probably on his family stake. Low personal media profile; best route is via Torrent corporate communications or the company secretary (IR email above). Was 33 in May 2025.

name: Michael Walker
current_role: Founder, Karndean Designflooring (family-owned luxury vinyl flooring maker, Evesham, Worcestershire)
profile: Most likely Mike Walker, the flooring installer who started Karndean from his family home in 1973 and pioneered realistic wood- and stone-effect luxury vinyl tile. Karndean remains family-owned, has 500+ employees and offices worldwide, and opened in Australia in the early 1980s.
interesting_fact: Karndean's own history says Mike set out to make flooring more accessible and travelled the world for inspiration, pioneering authentic replication of real wood and stone species in vinyl.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days he went out on sales calls in his van with flooring samples and his Great Dane, Smokey.
notes: Identity inferred: the Rich List entry gives only 'Michael Walker, Flooring'; Karndean founder Mike Walker is the clear match (trademarks also filed under Michael Thomas Frederick Walker), but no source explicitly ties the two. Karndean's site refers to him as 'Mike'. Very low public profile; approach via Karndean corporate.

name: Austin Chandler Willis
current_role: CEO (since April 2022) and President, Willis Lease Finance Corporation (Nasdaq: WLFC); director since 2008
profile: Austin Willis is the son of founder Charles F. Willis and leads WLFC, a lessor of commercial jet engines, aircraft and aviation services. Before becoming CEO he founded parts business JT-Power (later sold to Willis Aeronautical Services), ran consultancy Aviation Management LLC, and served as SVP of corporate development. His wealth stems from his WLFC shareholding.
interesting_fact: He served in US Army special forces and says selection and deployments 'inoculated' him to stress; his grandfather was a WWII pilot turned airline executive and his father founded WLFC in the 1980s after flying refugees out of Vietnam.
deep_cut_fact: After a New York investment bank told him it mostly hired from the Ivy League (he called that 'both insulting and motivating'), he transferred to the London School of Economics. Later, starting his own parts business, he ran out of money and lived out of his truck before it found its footing.
notes: Engaging, candid interviewee (ISTAT Q&A); aviation-engine leasing and sustainable aviation are a natural energy-adjacent angle. WLFC's contact page lists only individual staff emails, so none are included; use corporate/IR via the site.

name: Javier Rodriguez
current_role: CEO, DaVita Inc. (since 2019); director, Gilead Sciences
profile: Mexican-born Javier J. Rodriguez joined DaVita's reimbursement department in 1998, rose through kidney-care operations and payor contracting, ran DaVita Kidney Care (2014-19) and became CEO of the Fortune 500 dialysis provider in 2019. Earlier he worked in finance at Baxter and in operations for CBS Marketing in Mexico City. Boston College BS, Harvard MBA; sits on Gilead's board.
interesting_fact: He started at DaVita in the reimbursement department and rose to CEO over two decades; he was named one of Hispanic Executive magazine's 2015 Top 10 Leaders.
deep_cut_fact: His work ethic came from his entrepreneur father: at eight he worked holidays in his dad's gift shop, then as a dishwasher and busboy at the restaurant his father opened, before being 'promoted to the big leagues, to waiter.' He credits his Jesuit high school for teaching him to care about others.
notes: Fortune 500 CEO; route via DaVita newsroom. He has given long-form interviews (Fortune 2023, Fierce Healthcare, Hispanic Executive), so he is open to media on kidney care, caregiving and AI. Still CEO per Q2 2026 results.

name: Mark Wakeford
current_role: Chairman, Evoenergy (UK solar/renewables installer); Strategy Director, Global Solar Council; Chair, West Midlands Solar Taskforce
profile: Cambridge-educated chartered civil engineer who spent 26 years as a director/MD of the Wakeford family's 150-year-old Rugby contractor Stepnell. In the 2022 demerger he and brother Richard took Evoenergy, Brackley Investments, Aspen Retirement and a PFI school contract. He is now a prominent solar advocate and former chairman of the National Federation of Builders.
interesting_fact: He hosts his own show, 'The Building Podcast with Mark Wakeford', interviewing construction-sector experts as 'CPD on the go'. He is a natural fit for an energy podcast given his solar-industry roles.
deep_cut_fact: Besides solar, he sits on the Construction Industry Robots Cooperative and is still a director of a PFI school project in Hereford. On splitting the family firm he said: 'Demerging a 150-year-old group has taken some time.'
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: an active solar advocate and podcaster himself, so a guest swap could work. The podcast page prints his LinkedIn as 'linked.com/in/markwakeford' (typo). info@ and X are Evoenergy company channels. Rich List entry shared with Tom Wakeford (cousin, Stepnell).
